title: ÆTHER: Neon Raja v3 (South Indian film sound)
story: A king rules a rain-soaked neon city of the future; this is his mass entry theme.

brief.notes: Jithesh 29 Oct 17:10 on v2: concept fine, 'music is pathetic, no Indian touch'; same day in another thread: 'all same Western music, I need that Indian touch, especially South Indian movie music'. v3 flips the balance: today's South Indian (Tamil/Telugu) film hero-elevation BGM leads (raga melody on nadaswaram, violin section with gamaka slides, thavil and mridangam groove, wordless male chorus), glossy modern production underneath; the retro synth is only the cyberpunk colour. Prompt mode so it gets music_v2. Rules kept: section 9 motif, mystery start, hook every 8-12 s, surprise, key lift.

prompt: A brand-new South Indian film hero-elevation BGM, the kind that plays when the king makes his mass entry in a big Tamil or Telugu movie today. Instrumental, no lyrics. The Indian sound leads clearly from start to end: a powerful nadaswaram plays a proud, catchy melody in raga Kiravani with deep gamaka slides; a big film violin section answers it with sweeping gamaka runs; thavil and mridangam drive the groove with fast, rolling South Indian patterns, joined by a huge modern cinematic kick and a deep sub bass; a wordless male chorus chants 'hey' and 'aa' on the hook like a temple crowd. Cyberpunk colour in the background only: a warm retro analog synth arpeggio and a neon-hum pad under the Indian instruments, never louder than them. Glossy, loud, modern film mix, about 100 BPM, C sharp minor. Structure: the very first second is a sharp nadaswaram cry over a deep boom; then the nadaswaram alone plays a rising three-note call (root, minor third, fifth, the last note bent up) over a soft synth arpeggio; at 8 seconds the thavil enters with a roll and the groove starts; a new section every 10 seconds, each landing on the hook played by a different instrument (nadaswaram, then violins, then chorus); at about 35 seconds a surprise: everything stops for one beat, then a mridangam-and-thavil drum showdown slams in double time; the last hook is lifted up a whole step and played biggest by nadaswaram, violins and chorus together, ending on one huge hit and the nadaswaram's three-note call. Not Western pop, not EDM, not synthwave-led, not ambient, no white-noise risers, no side-chain pumping, not old-fashioned folk recording.
